title: ENTRESTO (sacubitril and valsartan) tablets and ENTRESTO SPRINKLE oral pellets: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling, published in DailyMed (National Library of Medicine); structured product label version 25, effective 6 July 2026
funder: not stated. The document is prescribing information approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and published by the labeller, Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation.
result: A combination of a neprilysin inhibitor, sacubitril (metabolised to LBQ657), and the angiotensin receptor blocker valsartan; contraindicated with ACE inhibitors, within 36 hours of switching, because of increased angio-oedema risk, and after angio-oedema on an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker. PARADIGM-HF required sequential enalapril and sacubitril-valsartan run-in periods (median 15 and 29 days): 1102 patients (10.5%) left during the enalapril run-in, 5.6% for adverse events (renal dysfunction 1.7%, hyperkalaemia 1.7%, hypotension 1.4%), and a further 10.4% during the sacubitril-valsartan run-in; the label states that because of this run-in design the adverse reaction rates are lower than expected in practice. In the double-blind period (4203 against 4229 patients, median exposure 24 months), angio-oedema occurred in 0.5% on sacubitril-valsartan against 0.2% on enalapril, and in Black patients 2.4% against 0.5%; hypotension 18% against 12%, hyperkalaemia 12% against 14%, cough 9% against 13%, renal failure 5% against 5%; potassium above 5.5 mEq/l in about 16% and creatinine rise above 50% in about 16% of both groups. In cynomolgus monkeys, two weeks of treatment raised cerebrospinal fluid amyloid-beta 1-40, 1-42 and 1-38 without a rise in brain amyloid-beta.
